ordered_diagnoses: Ventricular tachycardia secondary to myocardial ischemia

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and evolving left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
Inducible angina at 50 W without ECG changes
Significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
New QTc prolongation to 500 ms
Severely reduced LVEF of 35% with akinesia of apical and mid-segments
key_facts: 67-year-old man
Hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Recent exercise stress test induced angina
ECG showed normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed LVEF of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
Coronary angiography demonstrated patent stents in the circumflex artery and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
Developed worsening chest pain after transfer to the intensive care unit
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3
Second angiogram showed subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
Treated with balloon angioplasty, relieving his pain
Developed recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
Required seven external shocks and 15 minutes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation

shortlist.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had hypertension and developed ventricular arrhythmias

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening chest pain, ECG changes, and significantly reduced LVEF after a stressful event, along with the characteristic echocardiographic findings of akinesia of apical segments and hyperkinesia of basal segments, is consistent with takotsubo cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The coronary angiography did not show any new occlusions, and the patient had recently undergone stenting

rejected.label: Stent thrombosis
rejected.why: The second angiogram showed patent stents

rejected.label: Ventricular tachycardia secondary to myocardial ischemia
rejected.why: Although the patient had ventricular tachycardia, it was not the primary diagnosis

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's LVEF was initially normal, and the reduction in LVEF was a late finding

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc prolongation was a new finding, likely secondary to the cardiac event

rejected.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: There is no mention of hypertrophy on the echocardiogram
